title: Zacchaeus, the Minas, and the Triumphal Entry

questions.question: When Jesus entered Jericho, who was the chief tax collector who was rich and was seeking to see who Jesus was?
options: Zacchaeus
Levi
Matthew
Cornelius
questions.explanation: Luke 19:2 (ESV): "And there was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector and was rich."

questions.question: Why could Zacchaeus not see Jesus on account of the crowd?
options: Because he was small in stature
Because the guards pushed him back violently
Because the dust was too thick from the travelers
Because he was blinded completely in one eye
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was small in stature
questions.explanation: Luke 19:3 (ESV): "And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, but on account of the crowd he could not, because he was small in stature."

questions.question: What did Zacchaeus do to see Jesus, who was to pass that way?
options: He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree
He paid a strong man to carry him on his shoulders
He stood upon the rooftop of a nearby inn
He bribed the front row to let him stand before them
questions.correctAnswer: He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree
questions.explanation: Luke 19:4 (ESV): "So he ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was about to pass that way."

questions.question: What did Jesus say when He came to the place and looked up at Zacchaeus in the tree?
options: "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today."
"Zacchaeus, your faith is a marvel; come down and be saved."
"What are you doing among the branches, you wealthy sinner?"
"Bring me a cup of water, for I am thirsty before entering your house."
questions.correctAnswer: "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:5 (ESV): "And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, 'Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today.'"

questions.question: In response to the crowd's grumbling that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner, what two promises did Zacchaeus make to the Lord?
options: He would give half of his goods to the poor, and if he defrauded anyone of anything, restore it fourfold
He would tithe twenty percent forever, and build a new synagogue
He would resign from being a tax collector, and give all to the temple immediately
He would follow him to Jerusalem, and fund his ministry perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: He would give half of his goods to the poor, and if he defrauded anyone of anything, restore it fourfold
questions.explanation: Luke 19:8 (ESV): "And Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, 'Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.'"

questions.question: Jesus declared: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to..." what?
options: "...save the lost."
"...call the sinners home."
"...destroy the works of darkness entirely."
"...redeem the nation of Israel."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:10 (ESV): "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."

questions.question: In the Parable of the Ten Minas, a nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom. What did his citizens do?
options: They hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, "We do not want this man to reign over us."
They rejoiced incredibly and threw a feast lasting seven days
They armed themselves against his return
They stole all the minas back from the servants
questions.correctAnswer: They hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, "We do not want this man to reign over us."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:14 (ESV): "But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'"

questions.question: When the nobleman returned as king, he called the servants to whom he gave the money. The first servant made ten minas more from his one. What was his reward?
options: Authority over ten cities
A seat at the king's immediate right hand
He was given half the king's treasury
A newly built mansion in the capital city
questions.explanation: Luke 19:17 (ESV): "And he said to him, 'Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.'"

questions.question: The wicked servant kept his mina laid away in a handkerchief out of fear, because he claimed the master was a severe man who takes what he did not deposit. What did the master command be done with his one mina?
options: "Take the mina from him, and give it to the one who has the ten minas."
"Throw the mina into the sea, for it is cursed by laziness."
"Give it to the poor weeping outside the gates."
"Melt the silver entirely and throw the man into prison."
questions.correctAnswer: "Take the mina from him, and give it to the one who has the ten minas."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:24 (ESV): "And he said to those who stood by, 'Take the mina from him, and give it to the one who has the ten minas.'"

questions.question: What did the returning king command to be done with those enemies who did not want him to reign over them?
options: "Bring them here and slaughter them before me."
"Drive them completely into the wilderness forever."
"Chain them deep in the lowest dungeon."
"Tax them until they surrender all they own."
questions.correctAnswer: "Bring them here and slaughter them before me."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:27 (ESV): "But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me."

questions.question: As Jesus approached Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, He sent two disciples to untie a colt on which no one has ever sat. If anyone asked why they were untying it, what were they to say?
options: "The Lord has need of it."
"It is for the King of the Jews."
"We are renting it for the Passover feast."
"It is required by the prophet of Nazareth."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:31 (ESV): "If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' you shall say this: 'The Lord has need of it.'"

questions.question: As Jesus rode the colt down the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of His disciples began to rejoice and praise God loudly. Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples." How did Jesus reply?
options: "I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out."
"The time for silence has truly passed in Israel."
"Do not halt the praise commanded by my Father in heaven."
"If they are quiet, the angels will take up their song entirely."
questions.correctAnswer: "I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out."
questions.explanation: Luke 19:40 (ESV): "He answered, 'I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out.'"

questions.question: When Jesus drew near and saw the city of Jerusalem, what was His emotional reaction?
options: He wept over it
He smiled with grand expectation
He fell silent and did not speak for hours
He raised his hands and cursed the walls
questions.explanation: Luke 19:41 (ESV): "And when he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it,"

questions.question: Why did Jesus say enemies would tear down Jerusalem to the ground and not leave one stone upon another?
options: Because they did not know the time of their visitation
Because the religious leaders built the temple with bloody money
Because Roman wrath could not be stopped eventually
Because the foundation of the city was corrupt continually
questions.correctAnswer: Because they did not know the time of their visitation
questions.explanation: Luke 19:44 (ESV): "and tear you down to the ground, you and your children within you. And they will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you did not know the time of your visitation."

questions.question: When Jesus entered the temple and began to drive out those who sold things, He quoted Scripture saying, "My house shall be a house of prayer," but they had made it what?
options: A den of robbers
A market of vile deceit
A stadium for the wealthy exclusively
A butcher's shop entirely
questions.explanation: Luke 19:46 (ESV): "saying to them, 'It is written, "My house shall be a house of prayer," but you have made it a den of robbers.'"

key_verse_text: "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
